key_insight: Froq enables safe speculative execution on live quantum states, reducing decoder-induced stalls without relying on quantum-state copying or rollback.
engineering_relevance: Compiler-guided recovery and resource-aware scheduling can shorten fault-tolerant quantum execution despite slow classical error-correction decoding.
method: Extend speculation beyond classical decoding to quantum operations.
Use compiler-assisted recovery contracts to track misprediction propagation.
Reserve recovery workspace and balance speculative gains against expected recovery costs at runtime.
evidence_signal: Across eight FTQC programs and 88 configurations, Froq reduced quantum-side time by 9.81%; reductions reached 18.34% across 45 configurations allowing concurrent predictions and peaked at 31.1% at code distance d=21 under limited resources.
watch_item: Benefits depend on available recovery workspace and prediction concurrency; the abstract does not establish performance on physical quantum hardware.
paper_title: Froq: Safe Speculative Execution on Live Quantum States for FTQC
